objective.statement: Give every agent client session one stable session-unique swarm consumer identity instead of bare client or root names.
objective.measure: The shared hook resolves consumer identity by explicit override, SE_WORKSPACE_OWNER, hook payload session id, then a persisted per-client+workspace UUID; poll, ack, and sender share that identity; deferred-ack state is keyed by consumer so concurrent same-client sessions never cross-acknowledge.

need.statement: Give every agent client session one stable session-unique swarm consumer identity instead of bare client or root names.
stakeholders: Concurrent agent sessions on the devbox that share the repo-memory swarm bus and the deferred-ack hook state directory.
need.baseline: consumerFor maps Codex to the bare identity "root" and every other client to its bare client name, so concurrent sessions of one client share a consumer cursor and one deferred-ack state file, letting one session acknowledge another session's deliveries.
need.consequence_of_no_action: Cross-session acknowledgement loses durable messages, same-client sessions steal each other's cursor position, and the Codex root identity collides with the bus-era root consumer.
assumptions: Hook payloads carry session_id, sessionId, or conversation_id for session-scoped events on supported clients.
alternatives_considered: Keep bare client identities and lock the shared state file
Derive identity from process id per invocation
Migrate legacy state files onto the new consumer

purpose: Give every agent client session one stable session-unique swarm consumer identity instead of bare client or root names.
consumer: Concurrent agent sessions on the devbox that share the repo-memory swarm bus and the deferred-ack hook state directory.
contract: The shared hook resolves consumer identity by explicit REPO_MEMORY_SWARM_CONSUMER override, then SE_WORKSPACE_OWNER, then the hook payload session id, then a generated UUID persisted once per client+workspace; the payload session id is the first non-blank trimmed value among payload.session_id, payload.sessionId, and payload.conversation_id, so a blank earlier alias never masks a valid later alias and non-string values (objects, arrays, booleans) count as absent; explicit override and owner values are authoritative full consumer identities with surrounding whitespace normalized (trimmed) and the remaining internal value and punctuation opaque (including forms such as kimi:<uuid>); only payload/fallback-derived identities normalize to client-lowercase plus a 32-hex-character SHA-256 digest (128 bits, collision-resistant, not mathematically unique) of the whole non-blank session id, so distinct session ids that share a normalized prefix still derive distinct consumers; poll, ack, and sender share the resolved identity; deferred-ack state files are keyed by a readable sanitized prefix plus a 128-bit digest of the full opaque consumer+workspace pair, so punctuation-equal consumers never merge ack state; legacy client-keyed state files stay untouched and are not used for ack state; an empty persisted fallback file self-heals once; SessionStart idempotency is bound to the resolved consumer; hook behavior stays fail-open.
failure_boundary: State-directory write failures fall back to an unpersisted per-invocation id for that invocation only; an empty or partial persisted fallback file left by a crashed writer is removed and rewritten once, and if healing fails the unpersisted per-invocation id still applies; gateway failures still fail open without acknowledging; the persisted per-client+workspace fallback is stable but NOT session-unique: without a payload session id, SE_WORKSPACE_OWNER, or REPO_MEMORY_SWARM_CONSUMER signal, concurrent sessions of one client in one workspace cannot be distinguished and share one consumer, cursor, and deferred-ack state file - this limitation is stated honestly and the stable fail-open fallback is preserved rather than patched with guessed client-specific environment variable names; the Engine repo-memory server contract is unchanged, so a brand-new consumer replays eligible broadcast/addressed history once. Breaking migration boundary: messages addressed server-side to legacy recipients (root or bare client names) are NOT delivered to the new digest-suffixed consumer because server polling is recipient-scoped (Engine repo-memory internal/store/swarm_messages.go:148 poll filter recipient=$3 OR 'all', :176 ack recipient boundary) - such messages are stranded, not redelivered; no dual-consumer or dual-ack migration is added in this slice, and operators must repost any still-needed legacy-addressed message.

evidence.description: Node contract tests prove precedence, first-non-blank alias selection, the 128-bit digest with a pinned known-answer vector, truthful explicit-identity whitespace semantics, non-string session ids treated as absent, per-session stability, prefix-collision resistance, blank session ids falling back, codex-is-not-root, sequential poll-to-ack continuity, distinct-consumer state-file isolation including equal sanitized prefixes without cross-ack, legacy client-keyed state byte-unchanged and unused for ack state, persisted fallback stability, single-heal of an empty fallback file, and consumer-bound SessionStart idempotency.

falsifier.claim: The change delivers the promised contract.

executable_check.description: Run the contract test; any failure falsifies the claim.

non_goals: Changing the Engine repo-memory PollSwarmMessages cursor-0 replay contract
Migrating or deleting legacy client-keyed state files
Acknowledging root-era deliveries as the new consumer
VCS operations, commits, landing, or Home Manager activation in this slice
invariants: One stable session-unique consumer per client session whenever a session signal (override, owner, or non-blank payload session id) is present
Derived identities use a 128-bit SHA-256 digest of the whole session id; explicit identities keep their internal value and punctuation opaque with only surrounding whitespace normalized
The payload session alias is the first non-blank trimmed value among session_id, sessionId, and conversation_id
Poll, ack, and sender use the same consumer across hook boundaries
Deferred-ack state is keyed by a readable prefix plus a 128-bit digest of the full opaque consumer+workspace pair, never by client or by the sanitized prefix alone
Legacy client-keyed state files are never written and are not used for ack state
An empty persisted fallback file is healed once rather than replaying fresh identities
SessionStart idempotency is bound to the resolved consumer

assumptions.statement: Engine repo-memory poll returns only messages addressed to the polling consumer or 'all' and starts a new consumer at cursor 0 (fabrics/tools/services/repo-memory/internal/store/swarm_messages.go:148), and ack enforces the same recipient boundary (swarm_messages.go:176), so each new session-unique consumer replays eligible broadcast/addressed history once while messages addressed to legacy recipients stay stranded.
assumptions.falsifier: Engine repo-memory source shows new consumers resuming from a persisted non-zero cursor, filtering already-seen history, or polling/acking across recipient boundaries.

assumptions.statement: Hook payloads carry session_id, sessionId, or conversation_id for session-scoped events on supported clients.
assumptions.falsifier: A supported client's hook payload lacks all three session id fields, in which case the persisted per-client+workspace fallback applies.

plane_constraints: Repo-memory owns durable messages and consumer cursors; the hook adapter owns identity resolution and deferred-ack state; no VCS or Home Manager activation in this slice.
